# local_active_queries leaks ~1 increment per 2.6 local requests (136 self-heals in 13 h) — capacity signal under-reports free slots

## Problem statement

The proxy's `local_active_queries` counter drifts **upward** and is repaired by the
self-healing clamp in `_recover_stuck_local_active_queries`
(`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:5718`), which logs
`local_active_queries counter recovered: reset from N to M (M active dispatch records)`
at WARNING on every repair tick (10 s). That clamp is the documented safety net from
**LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM** (high, completed) — *"False 'saturated' capacity signal starves
herdr downtime dispatcher overnight"* — plus the earlier leak fixes
LP-0MRIL2L3E0080OGC, LP-0MRMGUEVR0002S5W and LP-0MS8ZM98R000M8AN.

The leak is still occurring, at a high rate, on 2026-10-31:

- **136 recovery warnings** between 00:00 and 13:05 (`proxy.log-2026-10-31_00` 18,
  `proxy.log.2026-10-31_00` 60, `proxy.log.2026-10-31_06` 52, `proxy.log` 6).
- Delta distribution: 47× `2→1`, 18× `1→0`, 13× `3→2`, 8× `3→1`/`4→2`/`2→0`
  — i.e. almost always **one increment that was never decremented**.
- Context: **359 local streams** in the same period ⇒ roughly **one leaked increment per
  2.6 local requests** (not a rare race).

## Why it matters (impact chain)

`local_active_queries` is the proxy's in-flight local-request count. It is consumed by:

1. **`/llama/local/status`** — `available_slots`, `capacity_hint`, `active_query`. The
   herdr downtime worker's dispatch gate reads exactly these fields
   (`DOWNTIME_*_MIN_FREE_SLOTS`); an over-count reports `freeSlots: 0` and starves
   dispatch — the LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM symptom, which is why that item existed.
2. **Admission pricing** (`prefill_eta` occupancy) and the admission guard's
   `eta_occupancy_s` / `projected_wait_s`, so an over-count turns an admissible request
   into `eta_exceeds_budget`.
3. **Prefill saturation gating** (`prefill_gate_wait_ms`, `saturation=...`).

Observed in the same window as the parent finding: `12:42:45` and `12:42:55`
`WARNING local_active_queries counter recovered: reset from 3 to 2 (2 active dispatch
records)` while the pool has **2 slots** — the counter claimed three in-flight local
requests on a two-slot server, so admission and any slot reader saw a server that was
busy when it was not.

## Suspected coupling (verify, do not assume)

The measured-cache-deficit abort / eviction machinery is new since
LP-0MVV9JWL9003A6XR ("0 pre-change" for that class) and it releases leases and records
abandoned slots on a path that also ends the request
(`lease_released`, `abandoned_slot_recorded`, `local_eviction … reason=…`). A skipped
`_decrement_local_active_queries` on any of those early-exit paths would produce exactly
this pattern (one leaked increment per aborted request). LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ changes the
same paths, so this must be diagnosed rather than guessed: the item may turn into an AC
there instead of a separate fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — **Quantify**: a deterministic analysis over ≥24 h of proxy logs reports the
      recovery-warning count, the delta distribution, and the leak ratio per local stream
      (baseline: 136 warnings / 359 local streams for 2026-10-31 00:00–13:05, deltas 1
      dominant). Recorded as a comment on this item.
- [ ] AC2 — **Locate the leaking path(s)**: identify every early-exit path that ends a
      local request (normal completion, client cancel, deficit abort, eviction,
      no-progress watchdog, tenancy-lease reclaim, slot-assignment free, exception) and
      state for each whether it decrements the counter. Deliver as a table in a comment,
      with `file:line` for each release path.
- [ ] AC3 — **Fix**: every release path decrements exactly once (or the increment is
      moved so it cannot leak). A regression test drives each path and asserts the counter
      returns to its pre-request value — including the deficit-abort/eviction paths.
- [ ] AC4 — **Invariant test**: a concurrency test (≥3 parallel local streams, mixed
      success/abort/cancel) asserts the counter equals the number of active dispatch
      records at every step, so the recovery clamp never fires (assert zero
      `counter recovered` log lines).
- [ ] AC5 — **Observability**: keep the recovery WARNING (it is the detector) and add the
      leaking request's identifying fields (`session`, `turn`, dispatch-record id, release
      reason) to it when known, so a recurrence is diagnosable without a new investigation.
- [ ] AC6 — **Target**: over a ≥60 min post-fix window with real traffic, **0** recovery
      warnings; the 24 h figure recorded in AC1 must not recur. Evidence as a comment.
- [ ] AC7 — Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not remove or weaken the self-healing clamp — it is the last line of defence and the
  detector for this class.
- No change to admission pricing or slot-count semantics beyond making the counter
  accurate.
- If AC2 shows the leak is a benign read race in the clamp (not a missed decrement), prove
  it with evidence and downgrade the warning to debug with a documented rationale — either
  way the signal must end up actionable, not permanently noisy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_increment_local_active_queries` (~2926),
  `_decrement_local_active_queries`, `_recover_stuck_local_active_queries` (~5718),
  `_count_active_local_dispatch_records`.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` / the release paths (~1418, ~1586).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — eviction/lease-release and abort early-exits
  (`local_eviction`, `abandoned_slot_recorded`, `lease_released`).
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `/llama/local/status` payload.
- `proxy/tests/` — new regression + concurrency tests.

## Existing state (verified 2026-10-31)

- Clamp present with `local_active_queries > active_count` comparison; logs at WARNING.
- 136 warnings / 359 local streams in 13 h; deltas almost always 1.
- Prior related (all completed): LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM, LP-0MRIL2L3E0080OGC,
  LP-0MRMGUEVR0002S5W, LP-0MS8ZM98R000M8AN, LP-0MSAO0ZM4000QH3O.
- `wl search local_active_queries` → no open item covers the recurrence.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ** (critical) — deficit-abort 503 quarantines the whole
  `local-qwen3` entry; shares the eviction/abort release paths where this leak may live.
- **LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM** (high, completed) — the false-saturated signal + this clamp.
- **LP-0MVV9JWL9003A6XR** — eviction triage for the new `measured_cache_deficit` class.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — double decrement.** Tightening one path can double-release elsewhere; the
  AC4 invariant test must cover mixed paths, not just the fixed one.
- **Assumption.** The clamp's `active_count` (dispatch records) is the correct ground
  truth. If records are themselves created late, the clamp can undercount and reset a
  genuinely busy counter — AC2 must confirm the record/counter ordering explicitly.

## Review update (2026-10-31, independent proxy-log review — session `herdr-1793450762-1330301-22426`)

### AC1 baseline correction (measured, reproducible)

Recount over every timestamped 2026-10-31 log file
(`proxy.log.2026-10-31_003749`, `_004152`, `_00`, `_06`, live `proxy.log`; 00:00 → 13:14):

| file | `local_active_queries counter recovered` |
|---|---|
| `proxy.log.2026-10-31_003749` (00:00–00:37) | 2 |
| `proxy.log.2026-10-31_004152` (00:37–00:41) | 0 |
| `proxy.log.2026-10-31_00` (00:41–06:41) | 37 |
| `proxy.log.2026-10-31_06` (06:42–12:41) | 32 |
| `proxy.log` (12:42–13:14) | 5 |
| **total** | **76** |

- **76 recoveries in 13.2 h**, not 136 — the item's figure appears to include the
  previous-day file (`proxy.log-2026-10-31_00` spans 23:10–00:00, 13 more) and/or to
  double-count. Local streams finished in the same window: **355** ⇒ leak ratio **1 per
  4.7 local streams** (not 1 per 2.6). The defect is real and unchanged in kind; only the
  AC1/AC6 numbers need correcting so the post-fix target is measured against the right
  baseline.
- Delta distribution confirmed: **37× `2→1`**, 18× `1→0`, 11× `3→2`, 6× `3→1`, 3× `4→2`,
  1× `2→0` — i.e. essentially always a single un-decremented increment, as the item says.

### AC2 evidence: the leaking population is the abort/eviction path

For each of the 76 recoveries, the last 30 s of log was scanned for release-path signals:

| signal in the preceding 30 s | recoveries | share |
|---|---|---|
| `routing_skip_local` (any reason) | 57 | 75 % |
| local `Stream finished` | 46 | 61 % |
| **`measured_cache_abort`** | **29** | **38 %** |
| `lease_released` | 27 | 36 % |
| **`local_eviction` / `local_eviction_after_acceptance`** | **27 / 23** | **36 % / 30 %** |
| `client_disconnect` | 14 | 18 % |
| `slot_save failed … ReadTimeout` | 10 | 13 % |
| `abandoned_slot_recorded` | 9 | 12 % |
| no signal at all | 9 | 12 % |

The dominant antecedent is the **deficit-abort / eviction release path** — the same lines
LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ rewrites for AC1/AC4. `client_disconnect` (18 %) and `ReadTimeout`
(13 %) are second-order candidates; the 12 % with no signal need dispatch-record ids
(AC5) to attribute.

### Additional acceptance criterion

- [ ] **AC8 — fold-or-prove against LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ, decided before either fix
      lands.** AC2's table must state, per path, whether the missing decrement is on a
      path that LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ already modifies (deficit abort, eviction after
      acceptance, abandoned-slot release). If it is, implement the decrement inside that
      item (its AC1/AC4/AC8 tests must then also assert the counter invariant) and close
      this item as a duplicate with the evidence; if not, keep this item and add the
      offending path to its AC3 regression matrix. Either outcome is recorded on **both**
      items — the one thing not permitted is two independent edits to the same release
      lines (see this item's "double decrement" risk).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MSAO0ZM4000QH3O** – Fix lock ordering in _try_acquire_local_dispatch (completed)
- **LP-0MRB2ABNX008SF9P** – Bug: Proxy Logger Not Writing Runtime Output to Configured Log File (completed)
- **LP-0MTYL5K1S002M5QL** – Reclaim stale generating counters in cleanup loop (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — matched: 0mvwezcb0006wpbq, abandoned, abort, aborted, ac1 (+315 more)
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — matched: 0ms8zm98r000m8an, 0mvksxr4p001v0cm, 0mvwezcb0006wpbq, abandoned, abort (+312 more)
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: 0mvksxr4p001v0cm, abandoned, abort, aborted, ac1 (+310 more)

data.description:
## Goal

As the proxy operator I want T1 (the wire-contract proof below) to be a single
deterministic command with a machine-readable verdict, so that AC1/AC2/AC6 are
repeatable at any time instead of being a hand-run sequence that has to be
re-derived from prose — and so the *next* regression is caught by re-running
one command.

Parent: LP-0MVWBFN8L004Z3X8 (Phase A, test-first). Test procedure T1 in the
parent description is the specification.

## Why this is the first child (test-first)

The parent's T1 is currently a 9-step manual recipe with hard-coded `/tmp`
paths, a hand-tuned `* 7000` filler multiplier and no restore-on-failure
guarantee. `compaction_dry_run: false`, so an interrupted manual run leaves
`compaction_trigger_ratio: 0.7` live in production config. A harness with a
`finally` restore and a `--dry-run` mode is the prerequisite for executing
Phase A safely and for repeating it later.

## Scope

In scope:

- `scripts/compaction_bridge_probe.py`: preconditions, probe sizing, driving,
  header capture, marker verification, isolation check, restore, session delete,
  verdict JSON.
- `tests/test_compaction_bridge_probe.py`: unit tests for all pure helpers and
  the safety-critical paths.
- `--dry-run` (default-safe, CI-friendly) and `--live` (explicit opt-in).

Out of scope: the client mirror (Phase B), the bridge, base identity (Phase C).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `scripts/compaction_bridge_probe.py` runs T1 end to end in one command:
  preconditions (proxy `GET /v1/models` health, summariser reachable,
  `grep -c 'action=compact'` == 0), a unique pinned `x-session-id`, ported
  probe-body construction, repeated dispatch until `est_before` exceeds the
  trigger, response header + body capture, and `DELETE /admin/sessions/<id>`.
- AC2: The probe size is **computed, not hard-coded**: it calls
  `proxy.compaction.compaction_trigger_tokens` with the probe ratio
  (default 0.7) and asserts the computed trigger is 88,883 (per-slot clamp
  `262144 // 2 - 4096 = 126,976`), then sizes the body to land `est_before` in
  the band `[trigger + 1, 120000)` (the 120,000 warm-routing cap is a
  precondition guard, not a hard-coded constant).
- AC3: Config changes are always reverted. `compaction_trigger_ratio` is
  written to the probe ratio and restored to `0` in a `finally` block followed
  by `POST /admin/reload-config`, so an exception, timeout, Ctrl-C or failed
  criterion still leaves compaction disabled; the harness re-reads the config
  file afterwards and fails loudly if the restore did not take.
- AC4: `--dry-run` performs zero mutation and zero dispatch: it prints the
  computed trigger, target band, probe body size, chosen session id and the
  PlannedRequests, and exits `0`. It must be safe to run against a live proxy
  during a release.
- AC5: `--live` is required for any config write or dispatch; without it the
  harness refuses (non-zero exit, explicit message). The harness also requires
  an explicit `--no-batch-in-flight` acknowledgement so the "do not run during
  a release or audit batch" rule is enforced by the tool, not by memory.
- AC6: Marker round-trip is asserted verbatim: the `X-Compaction-Marker` base64
  decodes as UTF-8, starts exactly with `_SUMMARY_MARKER`, ends exactly with
  `_SUMMARY_MARKER_END`, and is non-empty; a failure records the decoded first
  and last 120 characters (never the whole body) for the evidence trail.
- AC7: The verdict is machine-readable JSON: booleans for criteria A (four
  headers present), B (marker round-trip), C (proxy logged live compaction),
  D (isolation — no other session compacted), E (config restored), plus the
  evidence file paths and the probe session id. Exit code is non-zero when any
  criterion is false.
- AC8: The redacted header dump written to the evidence directory keeps the
  marker's **length** and its decoded first/last line but not the marker body,
  matching the parent's "Evidence to attach on closure" requirement.
- AC9: Unit tests in `tests/test_compaction_bridge_probe.py` cover: trigger and
  body-size computation at ratios 0, 0.7 and 1.0; the header-parse matrix
  (all present / one missing / malformed base64 / non-numeric counts / wrong
  `occurred` value); the isolation filter (probe session excluded, a foreign
  session flagged as a failure); restore-on-exception; dry-run makes no
  network or filesystem-config calls (both stubbed and asserted un-called).
- AC10: The harness is never executed by the default test suite (it flips live
  config); the suite only exercises the unit tests and `--dry-run`.

## Minimal Implementation

- Reuse, do not reimplement: `proxy.compaction.compaction_trigger_tokens`,
  `compaction_target_tokens`, `_SUMMARY_MARKER` / `_SUMMARY_MARKER_END`,
  `proxy.utils.load_config`, and the existing `--json` conventions of
  `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py` (argparse + verdict artefact +
  non-zero exit on failure).
- Structure the script as thin `main()` over pure helpers
  (`compute_probe_plan`, `parse_compaction_headers`, `check_isolation`,
  `redact_headers`, `restore_config`) so every unit test targets a helper, not
  `main()`. `--dry-run` exercises the same helper chain without the I/O.
- Drive requests with `httpx` (already a proxy dependency) rather than `curl`,
  so header capture is exact and the marker bytes are not shell-mangled.
- Write evidence into a caller-supplied `--evidence-dir` (default
  `docs/dev/compaction-bridge-probe-<ts>/`) so Phase A artefacts are
  reviewable and attachable to the parent, not stranded in `/tmp`.

## Deliverables

- `scripts/compaction_bridge_probe.py` (`--dry-run` / `--live`).
- `tests/test_compaction_bridge_probe.py`.
- Evidence directory layout documented in `--help`.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/compaction_bridge_probe.py`
- `tests/test_compaction_bridge_probe.py`
- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `docs/session-compaction-design.md`

## Evidence (verified during planning)

- `compaction_trigger_tokens("medium", config)` with `ratio=0.7`,
  `local_model_ctx_size=262144`, `slots=2` returns **88883** (verified
  2026-10-31 in this worktree; the parent's arithmetic is correct).
- `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold = 120000` (the probe's upper bound).
- `server.compaction_trigger_ratio: 0`, `server.compaction_dry_run: false`.

## Dependencies

None. Prerequisite for the T1 execution child.

data.description:
## Goal

As the proxy operator I want one INFO log line per compaction-header emission
(and one distinguishable line when compaction was evaluated but emitted
nothing), so that reading the proxy log tells me whether the signal was
emitted at all — closing secondary finding 2 of the parent ("Header emission
logs nothing ... a loaded-but-idle extension is indistinguishable from a broken
one") and satisfying AC4's proxy half.

Parent: LP-0MVWBFN8L004Z3X8. Unconditional — this is required whether or not
Phase A/B pass.

## Current state (verified during planning)

- `proxy/proxy/router.py:397` `_build_compaction_headers()` returns `{}` or the
  header dict; the only log statement in it is
  `logger.debug("Failed to build compaction headers; omitting", ...)` on the
  exception path (`router.py:430`). The success path logs nothing.
- `router.py:2336` applies it with `outgoing_headers.update(...)` on the
  streaming path; a second site near `router.py:3551` covers the buffered path.
- `router_helpers.py:6218` already logs `session_compaction applied
  session=… priority=… est_before=… est_after=…` — but that line proves
  *compaction happened*, not that *headers were emitted*. The two can diverge
  (e.g. `compaction_summary_text` empty → no headers, compaction still
  applied).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: On the live-applied path, exactly one INFO line per response is logged:
  `compaction_headers emitted session=<id8> turns_summarized=<n>
  recent_turns_kept=<k> marker_chars=<len>`. It is logged once per response on
  both the streaming (SSE) and buffered response paths — never once per SSE
  chunk.
- AC2: A response that evaluated compaction but emitted no headers logs exactly
  one line naming the reason, distinguishable from "emitted": one of
  `compaction_headers none reason=disabled|below_trigger|noop|dry_run|
  remote_with_guidance|no_summary_text|build_failed`. `no_summary_text` covers
  the real divergence case (compaction applied, summary missing) and
  `build_failed` covers the exception path.
- AC3: No header-emission line is emitted for requests that never reach the
  compaction path (e.g. remote dispatch with no session), keeping router log
  volume unchanged for the overwhelmingly common `compaction_disabled` case at
  a rate that permits long-window analysis (the `session_compaction applied`
  line already fires per compacted request; the new line must not multiply
  log volume for non-compaction traffic).
- AC4: The fail-safe contract is unchanged and better observed: an exception
  while building headers still yields no headers and never changes dispatch,
  but is now logged at **WARNING** with `exc_info=True` (was `debug`), so a
  silently broken emission is visible in normal operation.
- AC5: Header names, values and encodings are untouched:
  `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py` passes **unmodified**.
- AC6: Unit tests assert: the AC1 line and each field on both response paths;
  exactly one AC1 line per response with a multi-chunk SSE stream; the AC2
  reason line for `disabled` / `below_trigger` / `dry_run` /
  `remote_with_guidance` / `no_summary_text`; WARNING + `exc_info` on the
  exception path; and that a logging failure cannot raise out of the emission
  path (fail-safe preserved).
- AC7: No marker text, no summary body and no message content appear in any
  log line — only ids, counts and lengths.
- (Parent AC4) the proxy logs one INFO per header emission (session, `turns_summarized`, `recent_turns_kept`, marker length) and the bridge logs one line per signal capture and one per reshape. A reader of the logs can tell "no signal emitted" from "signal emitted, bridge ignored it".

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a module-level helper in `proxy/proxy/router.py` next to
  `_build_compaction_headers` — e.g. `_log_compaction_headers(session_id,
  headers, reason=None)` — and call it from the two `outgoing_headers.update(
  _build_compaction_headers(...))` sites, so the accounting is in one place
  and both paths are testable with the existing `_mock_upstream_response`
  fixtures.
- Derive `reason` where the decision is already known rather than re-deriving
  it: `_build_compaction_headers` can return `(headers, reason)` internally
  while keeping its public single-dict behaviour, or the caller can read
  `session_result["compaction_reason"]` / `compaction_applied`. Prefer the
  minimal change that does not alter the contract test's public seam.
- Session id is already available at both call sites (`session_id`); truncate
  to 8 chars like the existing `session_compaction applied` line does, so
  operator greps work across both lines.
- `marker_chars` is `len(marker_b64)` (the header value length), which is what
  the parent's AC4 asks for ("marker length").

## Deliverables

- Emission telemetry in `proxy/proxy/router.py` on both response paths.
- Unit tests in `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py` (extend) or
  a new `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_telemetry.py` (preferred: keeps the
  frozen contract file untouched per AC5).

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_telemetry.py`
- `docs/session-compaction-design.md`

## Dependencies

None. Required by the T1 execution child (its pass criteria C/D are read from
these lines) and by the parent's AC4.

## Goal

As the proxy operator I want the client-side bridge to log one line per
captured compaction signal and one line per reshape attempt, so that a
loaded-but-idle extension (bridge installed, no signal ever arrives) is
distinguishable from a broken one (signal arrived, bridge did nothing) —
satisfying AC4's client half and making the parent's pass criterion D
(ordering evidence) observable.

Parent: LP-0MVWBFN8L004Z3X8. Unconditional — required whether or not Phase B
passes.

## Cross-repo constraint (read first)

This work lands in the **SorraAgents** repository, not this one:

- code: `~/projects/SorraAgents/pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/`
  (`index.ts` adapter + `compaction-bridge.js` pure core),
- tests: `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`,
- loaded via the symlink `~/.pi/agent/extensions/proxy-compaction-bridge` →
  that directory (verified present 2026-10-31), so no reinstall is needed
  beyond `/reload` inside pi.

The commit hash in SorraAgents must be recorded on this child and on the
parent, so the client half of AC4 is traceable from the LP item. Do not copy
the bridge into this repository.

## Current state (verified during planning)

- `compaction-bridge.js` has no logging at all: `handleResponse` returns a
  boolean, `reshape` returns a list or `null`. Neither reports why.
- `index.ts` wires `after_provider_response` and `context` and silently
  returns on a stale ctx / missing signal.
- There is no `ctx.ui` in print or JSON mode (`docs/extensions.md`), so
  `ctx.ui.notify` cannot be the logging channel — headless T2 would lose it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: One line per **captured** signal, emitted from the pure core:
  `compaction-bridge signal captured session=<id8> turns_summarized=<n>
  recent_turns_kept=<k> marker_chars=<len>`.
- AC2: One line per **reshape attempt**:
  - applied: `compaction-bridge reshaped <X>-><Y> messages session=<id8>`
    with `Y < X`,
  - not applicable: `compaction-bridge no signal — passthrough session=<id8>`
    (state absent) — the "loaded but idle" line, and
  - anomalous signal (fewer turns than `turnsSummarized`):
    `compaction-bridge reshape refused reason=insufficient_turns session=<id8>`.
- AC3: Exactly one line per event: `handleResponse` logs once whether or not a
  signal was parsed (no-signal case logs at most once per response, and is
  rate-limited to one line per session per turn so an idle session does not
  spam), and `reshape` logs once per `context` event.
- AC4: Works in every pi mode (interactive, RPC, JSON, print): no `ctx.ui`
  dependency. Lines go to **stderr** and, when
  `PROXY_COMPACTION_BRIDGE_LOG` is set, are appended to that file, one line
  each. The default channel and the optional file path are documented in the
  extension README.
- AC5: No marker text, no message content and no summary body in any line —
  session id (truncated to 8), counts and lengths only.
- AC6: Logging never changes behaviour and never throws: the logger is
  injected into `createCompactionBridge({ log })` with a no-op default, so the
  pure module stays dependency-free and a hostile/throwing logger leaves
  parse/reshape results identical.
- AC7: `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs` extended to assert: the AC1 line
  and its fields; the AC2 applied / passthrough / refused lines; the AC3
  one-line-per-event rule including the idle no-spam case; the AC5 no-body
  guarantee (assert the marker string does not appear in any captured line);
  and AC6 (identical `parseCompactionSignal` / `reshapeContext` results with a
  no-op logger vs a throwing logger). All pre-existing bridge tests stay green
  unmodified.
- AC8: README documents the exact log lines, the `PROXY_COMPACTION_BRIDGE_LOG`
  variable, and the grep recipe used by T2's criterion D.
- (Parent AC4) the proxy logs one INFO per header emission (session, `turns_summarized`, `recent_turns_kept`, marker length) and the bridge logs one line per signal capture and one per reshape. A reader of the logs can tell "no signal emitted" from "signal emitted, bridge ignored it".

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a `log` option to `createCompactionBridge({ log } = {})` defaulting to a
  no-op; the default writer lives in `index.ts` (adapter layer), keeping
  `compaction-bridge.js` free of `fs`/`process` imports except behind an
  injected function.
- Emit from inside `handleResponse` / `reshape` where the decision is already
  made — no re-parsing, no extra state.
- Idle rate-limiting is one `Set` of session ids already logged for
  passthrough, cleared when a signal is captured for that session (keeps the
  module dependency-free and the logic pure).
- Keep the existing public surface (`handleResponse` boolean, `reshape` list or
  null) unchanged so `index.ts` and the tests need no behavioural edits.
- Run `node --test` for the extension's unit test only via the test skill
  (`/skill:test` scope) — not ad-hoc.

## Deliverables

- `compaction-bridge.js` telemetry + injected logger.
- `index.ts` default logger wiring (stderr + optional file).
- `README.md` log-line documentation.
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs` extended coverage.
- SorraAgents commit hash recorded on this item.

**Key Files:**

- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/README.md`
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`

## Dependencies

None. Required by the T2 execution child (pass criterion D reads these lines).

## Goal

**Conditional.** If Phase A or Phase B fails because the client's rebuilt base
is not recognised as the proxy's base, implement base identity so the
divergence is detected explicitly (with a base id) instead of degrading
silently into `history_mismatch` and a from-scratch re-summarisation.

Parent: LP-0MVWBFN8L004Z3X8, Phase C + AC5. **Do not implement speculatively**
— this child exists so the repair is scoped and ready, and must be closed as
"not needed" when both T1 and T2 pass.

## Gate (must be checked before any code)

- If `Phase A verdict: PASS` **and** `Phase B verdict: PASS` → close this child
  with `--reason "Not needed: Phase A and Phase B both PASS (<verdict links>);
  AC5 remains unmet by design because no divergence was observed"` and change
  no code.
- Otherwise implement exactly the failing link. Phase A fail ⇒ the producer
  contract is the defect (no base id is meaningful yet; fix the link named on
  the T1 child and re-run T1 instead of building the handshake). Phase B fail
  with a recorded fail signature ⇒ implement the handshake below.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The proxy emits `X-Compaction-Base-Id` with the compaction header set:
  a stable hash (SHA-256, first 16 hex chars) of the **exact** compacted message
  list it dispatched; the same list always yields the same id and any change to
  roles, order or content changes it. The hash input/serialisation is
  documented in a docstring so the client can reproduce it.
- AC2: The proxy accepts `X-Dispatch-Base-Id` on the request. On a match it
  adopts the client's base instead of re-summarising (no CREATION
  re-summarisation) and logs
  `compaction_base adopt session=<id8> base=<id8>` at INFO.
- AC3: On a mismatch the proxy logs one WARNING naming both ids
  (`compaction_base mismatch session=<id8> proxy_base=<id8>
  client_base=<id8>`), re-signals once (emits the header set again on that
  response), and does **not** report `history_mismatch` for this cause.
- AC4: A second consecutive divergence for the same session stops mirroring for
  that session and logs the reason at WARNING
  (`compaction_base mirroring_off session=<id8> reason=second_divergence`);
  subsequent responses for that session carry no `X-Compaction-*` headers, so
  the client cannot loop.
- AC5: Clients that send no `X-Dispatch-Base-Id` behave exactly as today
  (contract preserved; `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py` green
  unmodified) — the handshake is additive and opt-in on the client side.
- AC6: No payload content, marker text or summary body appears in any log line
  or header beyond the existing base64 marker — only ids and counts.
- AC7: Unit tests cover: hash determinism and sensitivity (reordered turns,
  changed content, changed role); adopt-on-match (no summariser call — asserted
  with a summariser spy); single-mismatch re-signal (exactly one extra emission);
  second-divergence mirroring-off; absent-client-header passthrough; and that a
  malformed/truncated base id is treated as absent, not as a mismatch.
- AC8: The bridge (SorraAgents) sends `X-Dispatch-Base-Id` when it has captured
  a signal, and clears it when it clears state; its unit tests extend to cover
  send/clear. Recorded with the SorraAgents commit hash on this item.
- (Parent AC5) if the mirrored base diverges, the proxy detects it explicitly (base id mismatch, logged) instead of reporting `history_mismatch`, and re-signals exactly once; a second consecutive divergence stops mirroring for that session and logs why.

## Minimal Implementation

- Producer: compute the base id once, where the compacted list is built
  (`router_helpers.py` live-applied path), carry it on the session result
  alongside `compaction_summary_text`, and add it to
  `_build_compaction_headers`. Mismatch handling lives where the session store
  is compared (`session_manager.py` / `session.py`), reusing the existing
  `fallback_reason` plumbing rather than adding a second path.
- Client: reuse the existing per-session state map — store the id with the
  signal, add it to the outgoing header set in the dispatch path; no new
  persistence.
- Keep the "re-signal exactly once" counter in the existing per-session store,
  not in a new global.

## Deliverables

- Base-id emission + adoption/mismatch handling with unit tests.
- Bridge dispatch-header plumbing + tests.
- A paragraph in `docs/session-compaction-design.md` §7.3 describing the
  handshake and its stop condition.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session_manager.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js`

## Dependencies

Depends on the T2 execution child (its verdict is this child's gate).

# Optimize use of free tokens

## Problem statement

The `plan` model's fallback chain currently uses the MunitoAI free tier immediately after local Qwen3, before the timed opencode-go providers. This wastes free tokens during hours when paid/opencode models are available, instead of preserving them for the gap periods (e.g. 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC) when those models become unavailable.

## Users

- **Self-hosted proxy operator** (Map): wants to maximise free-token utilisation and minimise paid-model spend by ensuring free tokens are consumed only when costed models are unavailable.

## Current state

The `plan` fallback chain in `proxy/config.yaml` (7 providers):

1. `local-qwen3` — always available
2. `munitoai-free` — always available (resets at 00:00 UTC daily)
3. `opencode-go-3` — timed: 00:00-01:00, 04:00-06:00, 10:00-00:00
4. `opencode-go-2` — timed: same windows
5. `opencode-go` — timed: same windows
6. `munitoai` (paid) — always available
7. `deepseek-flash` — timed: same windows

During the 14-hour windows (00:00-01:00, 04:00-06:00, 10:00-00:00) when opencode-go entries are available, free tokens are consumed *first* (step 2) before the paid models. This is inefficient.

## Desired change

Move `munitoai-free` to **after** all timed opencode-go entries so that free tokens are consumed only during the gap periods when those models are unavailable (01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00).

Proposed new chain:

1. `local-qwen3` — always available
2. `opencode-go-3` — timed: 00:00-01:00, 04:00-06:00, 10:00-00:00
3. `opencode-go-2` — timed: same windows
4. `opencode-go` — timed: same windows
5. **`munitoai-free`** — always available (now sits in the gap)
6. `munitoai` (paid) — always available
7. `deepseek-flash` — timed: same windows

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `proxy/config.yaml` `plan` model's provider chain reorders `munitoai-free` to after the three `opencode-go` entries (positions 5-6 in the chain) and before `munitoai`/`deepseek-flash`.
2. During opencode-go availability windows (00:00-01:00, 04:00-06:00, 10:00-00:00), requests that would have hit `munitoai-free` now fall through to the opencode-go entries (or subsequent paid tiers if those are also unavailable).
3. During opencode-go gap periods (01:00-04:00, 06:00-10:00), requests fall through to `munitoai-free`, consuming free tokens during these windows.
4. All existing tests pass.
5. A comment on `munitoai-free` in `proxy/config.yaml` documents the repositioning rationale (referencing this work item).

## Constraints

- The change is config-only (reordering providers in `proxy/config.yaml`); no code changes are expected.
- Existing opencode-go `available_times` windows are unchanged.
- MunitoAI free-tier rate limits, cooldowns, and daily-quota handling remain as-is.

## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml` — the `plan` model's `providers` list must be reordered.

## Related work

- **LP-0MQYEMXTT009OEVQ** (Complete failover plan configuration with Pi instance integration) — established the original `plan` fallback chain.
- **LP-0MVT8SAZE00570J5** (Daily resets on MinutoAI) — documents the absolute daily-reset behaviour of the free tier.
- **LP-0MU1RXEPL005CK97** — documents the opencode-go availability window gaps (01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00).
- **LP-0MSHF16VG004ASWA** (Add opencode BigPickle to plan and code fallback chains) — introduced a free opencode tier (different from MunitoAI free).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Where should `munitoai-free` sit relative to the `munitoai` (paid) entry and `deepseek-flash`?
  Answer: After all opencode-go entries but before `munitoai` (paid) and `deepseek-flash`. The paid tiers are always available so should be tried before the free tier — this is the existing position, only the pre-free ordering changes.
  Source: analysis of current chain and work-item description.

- Q: Should the `munitoai-free` entry retain its existing configuration (rate limits, cooldowns, display_name)?
  Answer: Yes — only the chain ordering changes, not the entry's own properties.
  Source: work-item description states "Adjust the fallback chain", not reconfigure the entry.

## Goal

Record and, if wanted, close the one gap the fail-closed pushed-commit guard (LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9) cannot cover itself: the push that **lands** a new hook version still runs the previous hook, so a refused fast-forward on that single push can still gate a stale tree.

## Evidence (2026-10-31)

- `50167e00` (LP-0MVU94NJN008RAK0, the guard commit) was pushed after `implement.py finish` refused its fast-forward ("not a descendant of refs/remotes/origin/dev"); the main checkout still had the `v3` hook checked out, so the gate measured the stale tree and **no full-suite cache entry exists** for `50167e00`'s git state (verified by a `test_cache.compute_git_state()` key lookup).
- The very next `dev` push (`47bed454`, LP-0MVU94RN9006Z28Y) ran the `v4` hook and left full-scope exit-0 evidence at its own commit.

## Desired outcome

Decide whether to (a) leave as documented inherent behaviour (see the "Bootstrap note" in `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`), or (b) have `implement.py finish` refuse to push when its own fast-forward was skipped (framework change, SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3), which removes the trigger for every hook version, not just this one.

## Constraints

- Related/overlapping: LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3 (non-fast-forward retry path validates the wrong tree), SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3 (framework: push from the worktree / name the verified tree).
- No code change needed in this repo's hook.

## Goal (user story)

As on-call, I want the local contention queue to be visible as Prometheus
metrics (depth, wait seconds, and loss/fallback reason), so a single-slot
starvation regime is detectable live instead of only after a nightly log
analysis.

## Context

`docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` §6 (LP-0MVTV6GA8002P7QU) records this as an
uncovered gap: effect E6 (head-of-line blocking and queue waits) can only be
detected from the log-derived usage-analysis report (`queue_wait_ms` in the
prefill breakdown, `fallback_after_queue`), which is produced after the fact.
`proxy/proxy/metrics.py` publishes no contention-queue series, so nothing can
alert on a queue that fills up at one slot.

`discovered-from:LP-0MVTF26NP003KXKJ` (single-slot impact audit).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` exposes a queue-depth gauge, a queue-wait
  histogram (or summary) and a queue-loss counter carrying the canonical
  fall-through reason labels.
- AC2: The values are updated at the same points the queue admits, waits and
  drops a request (`proxy/proxy/router.py` contention-queue paths), so a
  gauge reading is never stale by more than one admission decision.
- AC3: A unit test drives the queue through admit / wait / loss and asserts
  the three series move, including the reason label.
- AC4: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` and the monitoring
  documentation list the new series.
- AC5: No change to queue behaviour, caps or config values — observability
  only.

data.description:
## Goal (user story)

As on-call, I want prefix reuse and cross-slot KV-cache steals visible as
metrics, so the thrash cost that a single-slot geometry introduces is
observable directly rather than inferred from a rising prefill-slot-seconds
ratio — **and I want that measurement turned into a decision**: either a
concrete recommendation for the additional work that would reduce the steal,
or an evidenced verdict that the steal is not real enough to act on.

## Context

`docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` §6 (LP-0MVTV6GA8002P7QU), effect E7: at one
slot every session maps to slot 0, so each session switch evicts the previous
prefix (recorded 95 % steal rate for two concurrent sessions at pool size 1).
Today `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` publishes no cache-reuse or steal series; the
cost is only visible indirectly through `prefill_slot_seconds` per served
turn in the usage-analysis report, and through log-side
`errors.slot_save_failed`.

That 95 % figure is quoted from a recorded investigation with no measurement
window (§5.8 of the same report lists "steal rate 95 % at one slot" as a claim
that **must** be re-measured before it is used to judge the geometry). This
item is the instrument that re-measures it, so it is also the item that has to
say whether the number is real.

`discovered-from:LP-0MVTF26NP003KXKJ` (single-slot impact audit).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A counter records prefix-cache reuse outcomes per local stream (reused
  vs cold), and a second counter records slot steals/evictions with the reason
  label already used by the save/restore path.
- AC2: Both series are published on the same lifecycle as the existing
  `llama_slots_*` gauges (started and stopped with the slot-metrics sampler,
  no ghost series after a backend restart).
- AC3: A unit test asserts the counters move on a reused prefix and on a
  steal, and that the label set is cleaned up on restart.
- AC4: The usage-analysis REFERENCE documents both series and how a
  single-slot regime would show up in them.
- AC5: No change to cache, save/restore or routing behaviour — observability
  only.
- AC6: **Steal verdict and recommendation.** Once the counters have run for at
  least one full 24 h window, a comment on this item records a decision, not
  just a number:
  - **Pre-registered threshold.** The decision rule is committed to the
    repository in the same change that lands the counters (in
    `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`, beside the new series) —
    i.e. *before* any measurement window is read — so the verdict cannot be
    retrofitted to the data. Recommended default, which may be tightened but
    not loosened after the fact: steal is **real** when either
    (a) ≥ 5 steal events per 100 local turns, or (b) measured aggregate
    prefix reuse ≤ 50 % for prompts > 20,000 tokens, sustained across at least
    two sessions sharing a pool of one, measured in the same window.
  - **The figures.** The comment states the measured prefix-reuse ratio and
    the steal/eviction rate per 100 local turns, with the window boundaries
    and the exact query (series plus expression) that produced them — enough
    that a reader can reproduce the number.
  - **If the steal is real:** the comment names the concrete follow-up work
    that would reduce it. At minimum it must name the *mechanism* (e.g. making
    KV save/restore cheap enough to be routine on a switch, or keeping a
    per-session prefix resident/paged so a switch does not evict it), the two
    metrics it would move and the direction expected, its effort band, and the
    pass/fail test that would show it worked. That work is filed as a
    `discovered-from:LP-0MVWPK2VH008YWBD` item (or a blocking child if it
    blocks this one) and linked from the comment; naming a mechanism without
    the metric that would prove it worked does not satisfy this AC.
  - **If it is not demonstrated:** the comment records that verdict explicitly
    with the measured figures and the threshold it failed, and comments on
    LP-0MVTF26NP003KXKJ so the single-slot report's E7 prediction (up to
    11.5 M re-prefilled tokens/day, from the quoted 95 % steal rate) and its
    §5.8 re-measurement row are marked refuted or downgraded rather than left
    standing.
  - **Either way** the verdict is stated in one line that a producer can act
    on without reading the table: "steal is real → do X" or "steal is not
    demonstrated in the measured window → no further work; E7 downgraded".

## Goal (user story)

As on-call, I want decode tokens/sec to be attributable to how many local
streams shared the decode batch, so the single-slot decode-latency prediction
(effects E3/E5) can be confirmed or refuted from metrics rather than reasoned
about.

## Context

`docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` §5.4 (E5) states the decode tail should
narrow at one slot because two streams no longer share the batch, and §5.8
lists this as unmeasurable with today's data. `llama_token_rate_gauge` is
labelled by `session_id` only (`proxy/proxy/metrics.py`), and the report's
`Decode speed` table is per stream, so nothing joins a decode rate to the
concurrency it was measured under.

`discovered-from:LP-0MVTF26NP003KXKJ` (single-slot impact audit).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A decode-rate histogram carries the concurrent-local-stream count (or
  pool occupancy at sample time) as a label, so a query can compute decode
  rate by concurrency bucket.
- AC2: The label/bucket source is the same slot-pool occupancy the sampler
  already reads (no second, divergent definition of concurrency).
- AC3: A unit test asserts the observed concurrency is attached to a sampled
  rate and that it reflects a two-stream and a one-stream case.
- AC4: A usage-analysis report metric derives decode tok/s per concurrency
  bucket and is documented in the REFERENCE.
- AC5: No change to scheduling or batching behaviour.

## Appendix

### Clarifying questions and answers

- Q: What is the authoritative concurrency source? A (plan): Use the existing
  `llama_slots_busy` gauge — it records "slots processing a task in the last
  successful /slots sample", which is the same pool occupancy the sampler
  reads. No new concurrency definition.
- Q: Does this change scheduling? A: No. AC5 requires no change to scheduling
  or batching behaviour. Only observability metrics are added.
- Q: What concurrency levels to bucket? A: Integer bucket counts (1, 2, 3+) —
  no complex histogram binning needed. The `llama_slots_busy` value at sample
  time is the count.

## Goal (user story)

As the operator, I want the local status paths to fail *closed* on an unknown
pool size instead of advertising three slots, so a missing config key can never
make capacity look larger than it is.

## Context

`docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` §1.2 item 5 and §3.4 row 26
(LP-0MVTV6GA8002P7QU) record that three call sites read
`server_cfg.get("session_slot_pool_size", 3) or 3`
(`proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — the `/llama/local/status` idle and
total-slot paths), so an absent key advertises three slots at either geometry.
The literal predates the single-slot question and is a latent observability
defect, not a live one: the configured value wins whenever the key is present.

`discovered-from:LP-0MVTF26NP003KXKJ` (single-slot impact audit).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The three call sites no longer fall back to a literal slot count: they
  derive the pool size from the same helper the rest of the proxy uses (or
  report `unknown`/`0` explicitly) and never invent `3`.
- AC2: A unit test asserts that with `session_slot_pool_size` absent the
  status payload does not advertise 3 slots, and that a configured value is
  reported unchanged.
- AC3: The comment that documents the fallback behaviour is updated.
- AC4: No behaviour change when the key is present (the configured value is
  still reported verbatim).

data.description:
# Provide a script that deploys Grafana, safely, so the memory dashboard is viewable

**Headline:** add one idempotent, verifiable script (`scripts/deploy_grafana.sh`)
that installs the documented Grafana version, provisions the Prometheus
datasource and the `LLama Server Memory` dashboard, installs the systemd user
unit from `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service`, exposes it on loopback plus
tailnet only, and sets a non-default admin password from a `0600` file — so that
"how do I view the dashboard?" has a one-command answer instead of a manual
runbook with three latent defects.

## Problem statement

Grafana is **not installed on this host at all** (`~/bin/grafana` does not
exist, no `grafana-server.service` unit, nothing listening on `:3000`), so the
dashboard in `monitoring/` cannot be viewed. Today the only route is the manual
runbook in `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` + `monitoring/README.md` § 4,
and that runbook carries defects that a script would otherwise inherit:

1. **Wildcard bind.** The documented unit passes no `http_addr`, so Grafana
   binds `:3000` on **all** interfaces — LAN-reachable, which is wider than the
   tailnet-only boundary Prometheus deliberately uses
   (`monitoring/README.md` § *Exposure boundary*).
2. **Default credentials.** The doc instructs `admin`/`admin` and its
   verification commands hard-code `curl -u admin:admin`; the README § 4 says
   "change the admin password first" as prose that nothing enforces.
3. **A dashboard provider path that cannot resolve.**
   `monitoring/grafana/dashboards/dashboards.yaml` sets
   `options.path: ${grafana_home}/conf/provisioning/dashboards`. Grafana
   interpolates `${...}` from the **process environment**, and no
   `grafana_home` variable exists, so the provider points at an unresolved path
   and the dashboard silently never loads. The existing test
   (`test_dashboard_provider_points_to_existing_dir`) *requires* the
   `${grafana_home}` token, so it protects the defect.
4. **Nothing verifies the outcome.** No test or script checks that the
   dashboard actually appears in Grafana's own API (`/api/search?type=dash-db`)
   or that its panels return data; the prior deployment item
   (LP-0MQR554O60033BGF) asserted "Grafana running" on paper while no
   Grafana was ever deployed.

## Users

Primary user: the operator of this host, who wants to open the memory dashboard
in a browser without hand-editing systemd units or re-deriving the exposure
decision each time.

User stories:

- As the host operator, I want **one command** that installs and starts Grafana
  with the Prometheus datasource and the `LLama Server Memory` dashboard
  already provisioned, so that I can open the dashboard immediately afterwards.
- As the host operator, I want the service bound to loopback and the tailnet and
  **never** to the LAN, with a non-default admin password held in a `0600`
  file, so that deploying a dashboard does not widen the attack surface.
- As the host operator, I want `--check` to tell me whether the deployment is
  healthy without changing anything, so that I can diagnose drift (unit
  disabled, service dead, datasource missing, dashboard absent) quickly.
- As a reviewer, I want the deploy path covered by tests that fail on the three
  defects above (wildcard bind, `admin/admin`, unresolvable provider path), so
  that they cannot silently return.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **A committed, idempotent script exists.**
   `scripts/deploy_grafana.sh` exists, is executable, declares its interface in
   a header comment, passes `bash -n` and `shellcheck` (already used by
   `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh`, `scripts/llama-bench.sh`), and follows the
   repository's install-script conventions (`set -euo pipefail`,
   `SCRIPT_DIR`/`REPO_ROOT` derivation, `--check` and `--quiet` flags as in
   `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`). Re-running it on an already-deployed host
   makes no change and exits `0`.

2. **It installs the documented Grafana version reproducibly.**
   The version is a single variable in the script and matches the version
   documented in `monitoring/README.md` (11.6.0); the tarball's published
   SHA-256 is verified before extraction; extraction lands in `~/bin/grafana`
   (the path `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` already uses) and the
   version is re-checked from the installed binary (`grafana-server -v`)
   afterwards. A checksum mismatch aborts non-zero without touching an existing
   installation.

3. **Provisioning files are installed, and the dashboard actually loads.**
   The script installs the datasource config, the dashboard provider config and
   the dashboard JSON into Grafana's provisioning directories, writing the
   provider `options.path` as a **concrete absolute path** (no unresolved
   `${grafana_home}` token). Success is asserted from Grafana's own API, not
   from file presence: `GET /api/health` reports `"database": "ok"`, the
   `Prometheus` datasource is present, and `GET /api/search?type=dash-db`
   returns the `LLama Server Memory` dashboard. The repo copies of
   `monitoring/grafana/dashboards/dashboards.yaml` and
   `monitoring/grafana_llama_memory_dashboard.json` stay the source of truth and
   the two dashboard JSON copies stay byte-identical.

4. **Exposure is loopback + tailnet, never LAN.** The installed unit/config
   binds Grafana to `127.0.0.1:3000` (the process never listens on a wildcard
   address), and tailnet access is provided by Tailscale's own listener rather
   than by widening Grafana's bind. The script derives the tailnet addresses at
   run time (`tailscale ip -4` / `ip -6`) instead of hard-coding them, degrades
   to loopback-only with a warning when Tailscale is down or `tailscale serve`
   is unavailable, and its own verification asserts that the LAN address
   (`192.168.0.199:3000`) is refused. No `admin`/`admin` credential appears
   anywhere in the script, the unit doc or the verification commands.

5. **The admin password is generated once and never committed.** On first run
   the script generates a strong password into `~/.config/grafana/admin.pass`
   with `0600` permissions (creating the directory `0700`), points Grafana at it
   via a file-based secret setting (never on the command line, never in the unit
   file, never in the repo), and reuses it on subsequent runs. The `--check`
   mode verifies the file exists with safe permissions and that authentication
   with the stored credential succeeds, reporting the credential **path** only —
   the value is never printed or logged.

6. **The unit is installed from the documented unit, not copied.** The script
   installs `~/.config/systemd/user/grafana-server.service` by extracting the
   ```` ```ini ```` block from `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` (the
   `unit_from_doc` pattern the repo already documents for every other unit),
   then `daemon-reload`, `enable --now`, and reports `is-active`. It aborts with
   a clear message if Prometheus (`127.0.0.1:9090`) is not answering, since a
   dashboard with a dead datasource is worse than no dashboard. The unit doc is
   updated in the same commit so the repository and the running state cannot
   drift.

7. **`--check` is a real health probe with documented exit codes.** Exit `0`
   when installed, enabled and active, health `ok`, datasource present,
   dashboard present, password file safe, LAN refused; exit `1` with a
   per-check failure list otherwise; exit `0` with a "not deployed" report only
   when `--check` is asked to inspect an undeployed host and `--allow-absent` is
   passed. Behaviour on an undeployed host is asserted by a test.

8. **Tests cover the script and the three latent defects.**
   `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` (or a sibling module) gains
   behavioural tests that: run `bash -n` and `shellcheck` over the script; drive
   the unit-extraction helper against `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` and
   assert the extracted unit has no wildcard listen address and no inline
   credential; run the script's provider-config rendering and assert the emitted
   `options.path` is absolute and exists; and grep the script, unit doc and README
   for `admin:admin` (or a `GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin` form) and fail on
   any hit. Reintroducing any of the three defects must fail at least one test;
   the obsolete `test_dashboard_provider_points_to_existing_dir` token
   requirement is replaced by an assertion that the provider path resolves.

9. **Documentation matches reality.** `monitoring/README.md` § 4 becomes "deploy
   with `scripts/deploy_grafana.sh`", listing the script's commands, the exposure
   decision and the password-file location (path only); the "What runs here"
   table's `grafana-server.service` row stops saying "not running on this host"
   once deployed and instead documents how to start/stop/check it;
   `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` carries the binding, password and
   provisioning decisions the script implements; and any README section listing
   host scripts mentions the new one.

10. **The full project test suite passes** via `/skill:test`, with no
    regressions, and the change is exercised end-to-end once on this host
    (dashboard reachable over the tailnet, panels returning data for
    `gpu_gtt_used_bytes` and the proxy panels) with the outcome recorded in a
    comment on this item.

## Constraints

- **No new exporter, no Prometheus change.** `monitoring/prometheus.yml`, the
  rule files and the scrape jobs are untouched; this item only consumes
  `127.0.0.1:9090`.
- **Never widen the boundary.** No wildcard `:3000` bind, no LAN exposure, and
  no secrets in the repository, the unit file or the process command line.
- **No hand-edited units.** `~/.config/systemd/user/*.service` is produced from
  `docs/systemd/*.service`, never edited in place — the repository is the source
  of truth (`monitoring/README.md` § *Changing the boundary*).
- **No containers.** Host-first binary install, matching every other unit in
  this stack.
- **Downloaded artefact integrity is not optional.** A release tarball is only
  used after its published SHA-256 verifies.
- **Scripts live in `scripts/`**, use the repository's bash conventions, and
  degrade gracefully (never leave a half-installed unit enabled).
- UK English in all written output; **CHANGELOG.md is out of scope** (the ship
  pipeline manages it).

## Existing state (evidence, gathered 2026-10-31)

| Fact | Command / path | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| Grafana binary absent | `ls -d ~/bin/grafana` | *No such file or directory* |
| Grafana unit absent | `ls ~/.config/systemd/user/grafana-server.service` | *No such file or directory* |
| Service inactive, port free | `systemctl --user is-active grafana-server.service`; `ss -tln \| grep :3000` | `inactive`; nothing listening |
| Tailscale usable, `serve` unused | `tailscale serve status`; `tailscale ip -4/-6` | `No serve config`; `100.79.231.101`, `fd7a:115c:a1e0::9b33:e765` |
| Prometheus is the peer service | `ss -tln \| grep :9090` | `127.0.0.1:9090`, `100.79.231.101:9090`, `[fd7a:…]:9090` |
| Dashboard artefact | `monitoring/grafana_llama_memory_dashboard.json` | title `LLama Server Memory`, `version: 2`, panels: RSS, models loaded, 5xx rate, GPU memory (GTT + VRAM carve-out) |
| Provider path defect | `monitoring/grafana/dashboards/dashboards.yaml` | `options.path: ${grafana_home}/conf/provisioning/dashboards` |
| Test protecting the defect | `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py:666` | asserts the path starts with `${grafana_home}` or `/` |
| Weak unit test | `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py:928` | `TestGrafanaSystemdUnit` only checks the file exists, is section-valid and mentions "grafana" |
| Documented install path | `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` | `/home/rgardler/bin/grafana/bin/grafana-server --homepath=/home/rgardler/bin/grafana --config=…/conf/defaults.ini`; no `http_addr`; `cp`-based setup; verification uses `admin:admin` |

## Desired change

New `scripts/deploy_grafana.sh`:

```
Usage: scripts/deploy_grafana.sh [--check] [--allow-absent] [--quiet] [--version X.Y.Z]

  (default)        install + provision + enable + start + verify
  --check          verify only; never changes anything
  --allow-absent   with --check, exit 0 when Grafana is simply not deployed
  --quiet          report failures only
  --version        override the pinned Grafana version (default: 11.6.0)
```

Structure (mirrors `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`):

1. `install` — download + SHA-256 verify + extract to `~/bin/grafana`; create
   `~/.local/share/grafana/data`, `~/.local/state/grafana/logs`,
   `~/.config/grafana` (`0700`).
2. `secret` — generate `/etc`-free `~/.config/grafana/admin.pass` (`0600`,
   32-byte base64) if absent; never overwrite, never echo.
3. `provision` — write `conf/provisioning/datasources/datasources.yaml` from
   `monitoring/grafana/datasources/`, and `conf/provisioning/dashboards/`
   provider config from `monitoring/grafana/dashboards/dashboards.yaml` with
   `options.path` replaced by the real absolute directory, plus the dashboard
   JSON copies from `monitoring/`.
4. `unit` — extract the `ini` block from
   `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` into
   `~/.config/systemd/user/grafana-server.service`; `daemon-reload`;
   `enable --now`; `is-active`.
5. `expose` — `tailscale serve --bg --tcp=3000 http://127.0.0.1:3000` when
   Tailscale is up (with a warning + loopback-only fallback otherwise).
6. `verify` — `/api/health` = ok; datasource present; dashboard searchable by
   title; authenticated query through the datasource; `ss -tln` shows only
   loopback; LAN address refused.

Unit doc change: keep `ExecStart` as the documented binary path with
`--homepath`/`--config`, and add `Environment=` lines carrying only the two
binding overrides (`GF_SERVER_HTTP_ADDR=127.0.0.1`,
`GF_SERVER_HTTP_PORT=3000`) and the secret's **path**
(`GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD__FILE=%h/.config/grafana/admin.pass`). Neither the
secret value nor a second copy of it ever appears in the unit, the process
command line, or the journal.

## Key files (predicted)

- `scripts/deploy_grafana.sh` — new; the whole deployment above.
- `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` — binding + secret + provisioning flags;
  setup commands replaced by "run `scripts/deploy_grafana.sh`".
- `monitoring/grafana/dashboards/dashboards.yaml` — provider path that resolves.
- `monitoring/README.md` — § 4 rewritten around the script; "What runs here"
  table row updated.
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` — script tests, defect guards,
  `TestGrafanaSystemdUnit` strengthened, `test_dashboard_provider_points_to_existing_dir`
  replaced.
- `proxy/README.md` — script list entry (if it lists host scripts).

## Related work

- **LP-0MQR554O60033BGF** — Deploy Prometheus and Grafana instances (completed):
  its AC 2 says "Grafana running", but only Prometheus was ever deployed; this
  item closes that gap for real.
- **LP-0MVOHRLPB0086Q5T** — Grafana dashboard GPU VRAM panel queries
  `rocm_vram_*` (in_review): made the dashboard deployable-by-review (panel
  queries now match published series); this item is what makes it *viewable*.
  Its guard (`TestGrafanaDashboardVramPanel`) must keep passing.
- **LP-0MVO8CLCL00086NT** — deployable, tailnet-exposed Prometheus (epic): the
  exposure model this script must match.
- **LP-0MVO8DORX004P05G** — Docs: record the deployed monitoring stack and its
  tailnet-only exposure (completed): `monitoring/README.md` § 4, where the new
  commands belong.
- **LP-0MVQ6NQU9009LY2Y** — Stale monitoring references (open): adjacent docs
  churn; avoid conflicting edits to `proxy/README.md`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: exposure regression.** A convenience wildcard bind would silently undo
  the boundary work in LP-0MVO8CLCL00086NT. Mitigation: ACs 4 and 8 assert
  loopback-only listening and LAN refusal, and the unit doc carries the flag.
- **Risk: secret leakage.** A password in the command line is visible in
  `ps`/`systemctl cat`/journal. Mitigation: file-based secret with `0600`, value
  never printed; AC 5 and AC 8's grep guard.
- **Risk: a green script over a broken dashboard.** File-copy success does not
  mean Grafana loaded the dashboard (see the `${grafana_home}` defect).
  Mitigation: AC 3 asserts via `/api/search`; `--check` re-asserts.
- **Risk: half-installed host.** A failure between `enable` and `verify` leaves
  a crash-looping unit. Mitigation: install → provision → unit → start →
  verify ordering, with the unit enabled only after provisioning succeeds, and
  the failure path stopping the unit and naming the remediation.
- **Risk: upstream artefact unavailability.** Grafana tarball URLs move between
  versions. Mitigation: single pinned version variable, checksum verification,
  and a clear abort message; the script never falls back to an unverified
  download.
- **Assumption:** `tailscale serve` is acceptable for tailnet exposure and the
  tailnet permits it (no serve config exists today; HTTPS certs may need
  enabling in the admin console — see open questions). Fallback is
  `http_addr=<tailnet IPv4>`, which loses loopback access and is therefore the
  documented second choice, not the default.
- **Assumption:** Grafana remains a single-operator, unauthenticated-to-the-
  tailnet service like Prometheus; no Alertmanager, no LDAP, no orgs.
- **Scope-creep watch:** proxy-side metric defects are out of scope
  (`llama_process_rss_bytes` publishing `0` is LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48 territory);
  a GTT-as-fraction panel remains the open follow-up noted in
  LP-0MVOHRLPB0086Q5T. Neither is fixed here.

## Open questions (non-blocking) and decisions taken

- **Q: How is tailnet exposure provided?** — **Decision (agent, recommended):**
  bind Grafana to `127.0.0.1:3000` only and publish it with `tailscale serve`
  (`--bg --tcp=3000`), because Grafana's `http_addr` accepts a *single* address
  and cannot reproduce Prometheus's loopback+tailnet multi-bind. This keeps the
  process loopback-only (the principle behind the exporters) and puts the
  network boundary in Tailscale, where the device authentication already lives.
  Fallback if `tailscale serve` is unavailable: `http_addr=<tailnet IPv4>`, with
  loopback access lost and documented as the trade-off. **Reviewer should say so
  now if they prefer the fallback.**
- **Q: Does the tailnet have HTTPS/MagicDNS enabled** (needed for
  `tailscale serve --https=443`)? — Unverified from the host; `--tcp=3000` is the
  cert-free default and avoids the dependency. If HTTPS is available, an
  `--https` mode can be a follow-up.
- **Q: Does the admin password live in a unit `EnvironmentFile` or a Grafana
  secret file?** — **Decision (agent):** use Grafana's file-based secret setting
  (`GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD__FILE`) pointing at the `0600` password file, so
  no secret is duplicated into a unit environment file that `systemctl cat`
  would print.
- **Q: Should the script manage a `grafana.ini`?** — **Decision (agent):** no;
  keep `--config` at `conf/defaults.ini` and express the two overrides
  (`http_addr`, `http_port`) plus the secret via environment variables in the
  documented unit, so the repository stays the single source of truth.
- **Q: Should the script touch Prometheus?** — No. It only probes
  `127.0.0.1:9090` and refuses to deploy against a dead datasource.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

Intake (2026-10-31) — no blocking questions asked: the operator's request was
"create a work item to build a script to deploy it", and the surrounding
evidence (absent install, documented-but-unsafe runbook, three latent defects,
`tailscale serve` unused) fixes the shape of the change. Decisions recorded
above for audit; each cites its evidence:

- *Which Grafana version?* — 11.6.0, the version `monitoring/README.md:23`
  documents and `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` assumes.
- *Where does the script live?* — `scripts/deploy_grafana.sh`, next to
  `install_git_hooks.sh` / `install-cron.sh` / `install-rocm.sh`, with the same
  `--check`/`--quiet` convention and `set -euo pipefail` header.
- *Why not simply commit a `grafana.ini`?* — because the repo's units are the
  source of truth and are installed by extracting the `ini` block from docs;
  a second config file would be another copy to drift.
- *How is "it worked" proven?* — Grafana's own APIs (`/api/health`,
  `/api/datasources`, `/api/search?type=dash-db`) plus a datasource query, not
  file presence; tests assert the script does this.
- *What about the LAN?* — refused by test, by `--check`, and by the unit's
  loopback bind; the LAN address `192.168.0.199:3000` must return `000`.

## Goal

As an operator I want `llama_slots_busy`, `llama_slots_sample_timestamp_seconds` and the `gpu:computing_workload:bool` recording rule to be live on this host, so `scripts/gpu_utilisation.py` reports computing/idle shares instead of `unknown 100%`.

## Context

discovered-from:LP-0MVT1O52G000LMC6. The code for both halves is merged on `dev` (LP-0MVT1O0VG00905EL publishes the slot gauges from the proxy `/metrics`; LP-0MVT1O4O1004ND6L adds the combined rule), but the running host services predate it. Verified 2026-10-31T21:08Z:

- `curl localhost:8000/metrics | grep llama_slots` returns only `llama_slots_query_failures_total` — the running proxy process has no slot gauges and no sampler loop.
- `curl 127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/rules` shows `gpu-compute.rules` without `gpu:computing_workload:bool`.
- Consequence: `python3 scripts/gpu_utilisation.py --window 1h` exits 4 with `unknown 100%` while the power figures resolve (power-only computing 12.4%, mean 56 W, max 122 W). That is the honest answer, not a CLI defect.

## Acceptance Criteria

# Reconcile a cache-served `available_slots` with a fresh slot-detail snapshot

## Summary

`GET /llama/local/status` pairs two independent `/slots` reads: the slot
**counts** (`_query_slots` → `available_slots` / `total_slots`) and the
per-slot **detail** (`_query_slots_detail` → `slots` / `capacity_hint`). Each
has its own graceful-degradation fallback, but only *detail* staleness is
reconciled against live proxy state. When the counts query fails and the
last-known counts cache is served (`slot_counts_stale=true`) while the detail
snapshot is fresh, the payload can report a free slot alongside a `saturated`
hint with nothing to tell a consumer which half to believe beyond the boolean
flag.

Found while triaging the two residual observations on
`LP-0MVUVHCAP004V0JI`; `discovered-from:LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM`. Not fixed there
by design ("neither is fixed inside this item").

## Evidence

Window 2026-10-29 20:00 → 2026-10-30 07:00 (`/var/log/llama-proxy`), the AC4
post-deploy night:

```text
2026-10-30 06:01:20,526 - INFO - status_request active_query=false available_slots=1 capacity_hint=saturated \
  ... latency_ms=714 ... slots_detail_stale=false slots_stale=true status_schema_version=4 total_slots=2
```

`slots_stale` is the union of `slot_counts_stale` and `slots_detail_stale`
(`proxy/proxy/handlers.py`), so `slots_stale=true` together with
`slots_detail_stale=false` means `slot_counts_stale=true`: the counts came from
`last_known_slot_counts()` because the fresh counts query failed, while the
detail was fresh.

Scale in that window (status-poll lines, `~`because the tool's own poll
selection differs slightly): 144 counts-stale-only polls, **89** of them
reporting `available_slots>0`, **54** of those `saturated`. So the pair
`available_slots>0` + `saturated` from a fossil count is not a one-off.

## Why it is a distinct gap

The handler reconciles only the mirror case (`proxy/proxy/handlers.py`, in
`get_llama_local_status`):

```python
if detail_stale and capacity_hint == "idle":
    # ... plus live in-flight work → raise available_slots
    available_slots = max(available_slots, total_slots - (live_local_requests or 0))
```

There is no counts-stale branch. A consumer that "polls this pair together and
acts on both" (the documented advice in
`proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`) can read `available_slots: 1` on a
fully occupied pool. The stale counts are *disclosed* (`slot_counts_stale`), so
the payload is not lying — but the pair is internally inconsistent and the
disclosure is easy to miss next to an authoritative-looking `capacity_hint`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The status payload never pairs a **cache-served** `available_slots` with a
  `saturated` / `abandoned_busy` `capacity_hint` derived from fresh detail:
  either the stale counts are reconciled (or withheld) when the detail snapshot
  is fresh and shows no free slot, or the inconsistency is documented as a
  consumer contract rule with a test that pins it.
- Deterministic test (mocked `/slots` counts failure + fresh detail snapshot,
  no live llama-server) reproducing the 06:01:20 shape and asserting the chosen
  behaviour; the existing stale-*detail* reconciliation test stays green
  (`proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py`).
- `slot_counts_stale` keeps its meaning (`true` only when the counts are cached)
  and the payload stays additive within the current `status_schema_version`.
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` consumer contract and
  `proxy/README.md` field table state the rule.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` (`get_llama_local_status`, counts/detail
  reconciliation)
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py`
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, `proxy/README.md`

## Notes

- Deliberately **not** the latency or lease-held `available_slots=1` shapes from
  the same residual: those were triaged as expected behaviour on
  `LP-0MVUVHCAP004V0JI` (a whole-poll latency envelope of up to 4 s, and
  `idle_leased` not being admission capacity).
data.title: Reconcile a cache-served available_slots with a fresh slot-detail snapshot

## Goal

As the operator, I want the local-share gap attributed to *throughput* (not routing) and the costed options ranked, so the parent's aggregate-share target is set against what the hardware can actually deliver.

## Measured basis (2026-11-01 13:12:48-14:00:03, 1788 requests, 58 sessions)

- Offered prompt load: 125.6M prompt tokens in 47.25 min = ~44,300 prompt tokens/s.
- Local delivered: 877,908 prompt tokens over 46 streams in 1,223 s of busy time = ~718 tok/s.
- Routing is NOT the binding constraint: the refusals decompose into prompt-cost verdicts (large_context_bypass 32.8% of fallbacks, resident_prefix_insufficient 24.7%, local_admission_guard 18.1% incl. prefill_budget_exceeded 193/314 guard rejects, context_too_large 16.6%), and only 76 of 314 guard refusals had a free prefill gate — of which all but 20 exceeded the queue budget on their own measured ETA.
- Ceiling: one serialised prefill gate x 2,820 s x ~718 tok/s = ~2.0M prompt tokens/window = 2.3x today's local tokens => local share ceiling ~5.8%. A >=10% share would need ~4.2M local prompt tokens, i.e. >2x the whole window's single-gate capacity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Costed options are compared: (a) session size/compaction (the median request is 57k new tokens; the top decile is >100k), (b) prefill-serialisation trade-off revisited with current-generation measurements, (c) model/quantisation or ctx/slot-geometry changes, (d) accepting the ~5.8% ceiling and re-scoping the parent's AC9 target. Each option carries a measured or explicitly-estimated tok/s and slot-hour cost.
- [ ] AC2 — A recommended target for the parent LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ AC9 share is proposed with the arithmetic, and the recommendation is recorded as a comment on the parent.
- [ ] AC3 — No routing/config change is made by this item (read-only evaluation; changes become children).

## Constraints

- Do not merely widen the local context window (LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM already evaluated the ctx-size axis).
- Do not use 'forcing full prompt re-processing' as evidence of a cache defect (expected on Qwen3.x hybrid/SWA, see project AGENTS.md).

## Goal

Attach the concurrent-stream count to the decode-rate histogram so decode tok/s can be queried by concurrency bucket, enabling E3/E5 single-slot impact to be verified from metrics rather than reasoned about.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A decode-rate histogram (`llama_token_rate_histogram`) carries the concurrent-local-stream count (or the pool occupancy at sample time) as a label, so a query can compute decode rate by concurrency bucket.
- AC2: The label source is the same slot-pool occupancy the sampler already reads (no second, divergent definition of concurrency). Use the existing `llama_slots_busy` gauge as the concurrency proxy.
- AC4: A usage-analysis report metric derives decode tok/s per concurrency bucket and is documented in the REFERENCE.
- AC5: No change to scheduling or batching behaviour.

## Implementation

1. **`proxy/proxy/metrics.py`**: Add a `llama_concurrent_streams` gauge (updated by the existing slot sampler) or read `llama_slots_busy` directly at observation time.
2. **`proxy/proxy/router.py`**: Add `concurrent_streams` label to the `llama_token_rate_histogram.observe()` call, reading the concurrency count from the same source as `llama_slots_busy`.

## Goal

As the proxy maintainer, I want a complete, evidence-based audit of every early-exit path that ends a local request — with a per-path verdict on whether it decrements `local_active_queries` exactly once — so the leaking path(s) can be fixed in one place without guessing, and so the AC8 fold-or-prove decision against LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ is settled on the current post-ship code.

## Acceptance Criteria

Parent criteria traced by this item (verbatim, so the automated AC-coverage review can match them):
- AC2 — **Locate the leaking path(s)**: identify every early-exit path that ends a local request (normal completion, client cancel, deficit abort, eviction, no-progress watchdog, tenancy-lease reclaim, slot-assignment free, exception) and state for each whether it decrements the counter. Deliver as a table in a comment, with `file:line` for each release path.
- AC8 — **fold-or-prove against LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ, decided before either fix lands.** AC2's table must state, per path, whether the missing decrement is on a path that LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ already modifies (deficit abort, eviction after acceptance, abandoned-slot release). If it is, implement the decrement inside that item (its AC1/AC4/AC8 tests must then also assert the counter invariant) and close this item as a duplicate with the evidence; if not, keep this item and add the offending path to its AC3 regression matrix. Either outcome is recorded on **both** items — the one thing not permitted is two independent edits to the same release lines (see this item's "double decrement" risk).


- [ ] **AC1 — per-path decrement table.** A comment on the parent item lists every released path: normal completion (`_cleanup_after_request`), client cancel (pre-first-byte `_release_client_disconnect_dispatch` + detached cleanup; post-first-byte disconnect), measured-cache-deficit abort (`_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch` → `_release_unserved_dispatch`), prefill-deadline release, eviction after acceptance, no-progress watchdog (orphan sweep), tenancy-lease reclaim / idle-timeout sweep, slot-assignment free, and the generic exception path. For each: `file:line`, decrement verdict (`exactly once` / `missing` / `double`), and the guard that makes it idempotent.
- [ ] **AC2 — counter/record ordering confirmed.** State explicitly (with file:line) whether the increment and record creation are atomic under the same lock (`_try_acquire_local_dispatch`, router_helpers.py ~4022–4135) so the recovery clamp's ground truth (`active` dispatch records) is valid; if records can be created late or removed early, say so and quantify the clamp's blind spot.

When this bug's fix is deployed it must **re-trigger the post-fix 24 h
validation** `LP-0MVVLKPBM007F6U6` (which is `blocked` on this item):

   windowed router-responder `GET /slots ... 500` count. Target: **0**.
